usage: 炒西洋菜 can function as the subject of a sentence, such as in "炒西洋菜好味" (Stir-fried watercress is tasty).
It can be used as an object, for example: "我想叫炒西洋菜" (I want to order stir-fried watercress).
炒西洋菜 is often paired with verbs related to cooking or ordering food, like '做' (make) or '叫' (order).
When talking about dishes in a restaurant context, 炒西洋菜 can be combined with price or quantity, e.g., "炒西洋菜一碟幾錢？" (How much is one plate of stir-fried watercress?).
You can use 炒西洋菜 in comparison sentences, like "炒西洋菜比炒菠菜好食" (Stir-fried watercress tastes better than stir-fried spinach).
